Translation of letter received from Chen Meu Hsuan,
Chinese lawyer, 430 Chekiang Road.
X D. 8149 (C.42C)

December 28, 1939.

To the Special Branch:

My client, Mrs. Huang Hsu Sz, states that
her husband, Huang Ching Meu(黄慶梅), was arrested
by the Police on October 27 but the nature of his
offence was not known to his family. Investigations
showed that he was arrested by the Special Branch and
detained at Chengtu Road Station where no one was allowed
to see him. He has been detained for two months and
has not been brought before the Court. Mrs. Huang Hsu Sz
inquires whether the prisoner can be released on bond,
otherwise he should be taken before the Court for a decision.
I am therefore requested to inquire from you.

(Signed) Chen Meu Hsuan(陈懋宣)

O.a.
Ignore
yR

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER OF POLICE 2 NOV 1939）

With reference to the attached report
from Louza Station on the arrest of two men one
of whom accused the other of being a murderer,
the arrested persons were brought to Special
Branch on the afternoon of October 27th for
interrogation.

Statements were taken from them which
substantially coincide with the facts submitted
in the Louza report.

Li Ying Ziao (李印樵), former editor
of the Modern Times (新時代) Newspaper, 309
Chungking Road, which was ordered to suspend
functioning by the Municipal Police on September
1st, 1939, and now sales manager of the Loh San
Suh (六卅) Medicine Hong, 309 Chungking Road,
who was kidnapped on September 23, 1939 by persons
from 76 Jessfield Road and released four days later
on promising to join the Wang Ching Wei Party and
take up editorship of a Party paper, was released
after questioning. He stated that he intended
to change his address and reside in French Concession
in future in order to avoid further incidents.

Wong Ching Mow (黄慶茂), the other
arrested man and an agent of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang
Anti-Comintern and National Salvation Army at 76
Jessfield Road, whose allegations against Li Ying
Ziao resulted in the arrest of both men, was detained

The following is the statement of Wong Ching Mow D.S.I. MacAdie
native of Yangchow taken by me D.S.I. Liao Chung Chien
at Special Branch on the 27-10-39 and interpreted by

My name is Wong Ching Mow (黄庆茂). I am aged
32 and a native of Yangchow. I am a member of the
Special Service Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-
Comintern and National Salvation Army and reside on the
premises of the Corps at 76 Jessfield Road.
At the age of 14, I came to Shanghai from Yangchow
and joined the Blanket Department of the Ewo Cotton Mill,
Yangtzeepoo, as a worker. In 1932, I resigned from the
mill of my own accord and joined the Special Branch of
the Public Safety Bureau as an agent through the recom-
mendation of my friend named Chiang Chi Hah (姜其赫).
Chiang was an ex-communist. He surrendered to the
Public Safety Bureau after he was arrested by the organ
in 1931. I became acquainted with him when he was
working in Ewo Cotton Mill in 1926. In that year he
was dismissed for participating in a strike.
I remained in the employ of the Public Safety Bureau
as an agent up to August, 1937 when the Sino-Japanese
hostilities broke out and I returned to Yangchow to join
my mother and wife, my father having died.
At the beginning of September 1939, I came to Shanghai
with a view to securing a job. On September, 15, I met
Soo (I do not know his full name), formerly a detective
of the Public Safety Bureau, on Jessfield Road. He told
me that a number of the ex-members of the P.S.B. were
working for the Wang Ching Wei clique and asked me if I
would join too. Being unemployed I accepted the

我叫黄庆茂（Wong Ching Mow，黄庆茂）。我今年32岁，扬州人。我是中国国民党反共救国军特别服务队的成员，居住在极司菲尔路76号该队队部内。
14岁时，我从扬州来到上海，进入杨树浦怡和纱厂（Ewo Cotton Mill）的被褥部当工人。1932年，我自愿从纱厂辞职，经朋友姜其赫（Chiang Chi Hah，姜其赫）推荐，加入公共安全局特务科担任特工。姜曾是共产党员。他在1931年被该机构逮捕后向公共安全局投诚。我在1926年他在怡和纱厂工作时与他相识。那一年他因参与罢工而被解雇。
我一直在公共安全局担任特工直至1937年8月中日敌对行动爆发，随后我返回扬州与母亲和妻子团聚，当时我父亲已去世。
1939年9月初，我来到上海寻找工作。9月15日，我在极司菲尔路遇到 Soo（我不知道他的全名），他曾是公共安全局的侦探。他告诉我，许多公共安全局的前成员正在为汪精卫派系工作，并问我是否也加入。由于失业，我接受了

Throughout last month I was obliged to come out
almost daily to the downtown area to purchase various
articles for office use, such as letter paper, envelopes,
ink, etc..

At about 10.30 a.m. October 27, Soo brought me to
Nanking Road to buy some clothing. At about 1 p.m.
when we were about to leave The Sun Company, Soo met
a friend of his, who was accompanied by a small girl.
They talked amicably for a while but when Soo requested
the man to come to 76 Jessfield Road, a heated argument
took place because the man stubbornly refused to comply
with the request. Soo then ordered me to summon a
police constable to have the person arrested, telling me
that the man was formerly a member of the Wang Ching
Wei clique and if he was permitted to go free, he might
attack us (members of Wang's clique) in future. Soo
also told me that I should go with the man to the Police
Station and he would later make arrangements to effect
the handing over of both the man and myself. After
issuing these instructions he immediately left for
Jessfield Road while I followed the man. Outside
The Sun Co. I told a police constable to place the
man under arrest on a pretext that he was suspected of
being concerned in a murder. At this juncture,
an altercation took place, the man charging me with

在上个月里，我几乎每天都要去市区购买各种办公用品，如信纸、信封、墨水等。

10月27日上午10点30分左右，Soo 带我去南京路买衣服。下午1点左右，当我们准备离开先施公司（The Sun Company）时，Soo 遇到了一位朋友，身边跟着一个小女孩。他们友好地交谈了一会儿，但当 Soo 要求那人去极司菲尔路76号时，发生了激烈的争吵，因为那人顽固地拒绝服从要求。Soo 随即命令我叫来一名巡捕将该人逮捕，并告诉我说那人曾是汪精卫派系的成员，如果让他自由离开，将来可能会攻击我们（汪派成员）。Soo 还告诉我，我应该随那人去巡捕房，他稍后会安排将那人和我都移交给他们。发出这些指令后，他立即前往极司菲尔路，而我则跟随那人。在先施公司外，我以涉嫌谋杀为由让一名巡捕逮捕了那人。就在此时，发生了争执，那人指控我

My Name is LI YING ZIAO. I am 30 years old,
a native of Peiping, residing at 309 Chungking Road,
the Loh San Suh ( 羅三蘇 ) Drug Hong, in which I
am employed as a member of the Sales Department. I was
previously the manager of the Sing Sz Tan (New Age)
( 新時代 ), a semi-monthly periodical which commenced
publication on April 5, 1939. It was registered with the
Municipal Police, Certificate No. C.426. When the
registration certificate was cancelled, the periodical
ceased publication on September 1, 1939.

On September 23, at 6 p.m., one of my fellow
countrymen called TSU SZ YUEN ( 朱士元 ) who is connected
with 76 Jessfield Road (Headquarters of the Special Service
Corps of the Chung Kuo Kuomintang Anti-Comintern and
National Salvation Army, a pro-Wang Ching Wei Organisation),
and another named CHANG ( 張 ) invited me to take supper
at Tsing Loong Restaurant, corner of Nanking and Yu Ya Ching
Roads. After we finished the supper, we left the
restaurant and boarded CHANG's private car (Licence No.
3741). They stated that they were going to Paramount
to dance. I told them I could not dance, but they requested
me to go there for amusement. After a short while, CHANG
stated that he would go back home for the purpose of changing
clothes before he went to Paramount. I asked CHANG about
his home address, and he told me that he was living somewhere
behind the Paramount. I later discovered that I was
driven to 76 Jessfield Road where I was detained for five

以下系由我，副督察长（D.S.I.）麦卡迪（MacAdie），于1939年10月28日在警察总部对北平籍人士李英樵（LI YING ZIAO）所作的供词记录，由高恩肯（Kao Yen Ken）担任翻译。

（批注：附S档案。因救国活动被停职。）

本人姓名为李英樵。现年30岁，北平人，居住于重庆路309号罗三苏（Loh San Suh）药行，受雇于该药行销售部。此前，我曾担任半月刊《新时代》（Sing Sz Tan）的经理，该刊物于1939年4月5日开始发行。该刊已在警务处注册，证书编号为C.426。当注册证书被注销后，该刊物于1939年9月1日停刊。

9月23日下午6时，我的同乡朱士元（TSU SZ YUEN，与极司菲尔路76号有关联，该处为中国国民党反共救国军特别服务总队总部，系拥护汪精卫的组织）以及另一名姓张（CHANG）的人，邀请我在南京路与虞洽卿路交界处的晋隆餐厅吃晚饭。晚饭后，我们离开餐厅，登上了张的私家车（牌照号码3741）。他们称要去百乐门跳舞。我告诉他们我不会跳舞，但他们请求我去那里消遣。过了一会儿，张说他在去百乐门之前要回家换衣服。我问张他的家庭住址，他告诉我他住在百乐门后面的某个地方。后来我发现我被带到了极司菲尔路76号，并在那里被拘留了五天

days between September 23 and September 27.
On the first day, one named LI ( ) approached
me and asked whether I was responsible for the publication
of the "Sing Sz Tan" and asked me about the number of
issues of the periodical. I replied accordingly and
added that the periodical had suspended publication on
September 1. LI then told me to stay there for a few
days and stated that he would detail persons to make
enquiries. He further stated that I would be allowed
to leave the place (76 Jessfield Road) should I be
found not to have taken part in any other activities,
but required me to reach an understanding of Mr. WANG CHING WEI's
cause while I was being detained. He also handed
over to me two books entitled "Speeches on Peace Movement
(和平運動言論)" made by WANG CHING WEI and
Recollection and Prospect"(回憶與前瞻) written by
CHOW FU HAI(周佛海).
No one approached me on the second day.
On the third day, one named TAN (譚) came to
see me and advised me to support Mr. WANG CHING WEI's
peace movement and abandon my sympathy towards the war
of resistance. I replied that I would take his advice
into consideration.
On the fourth day, LI again visited me and stated
that I could leave the place on September 27 as he asserted
I was found not to be concerned in any activities.

- 2 -

从9月23日至9月27日。
第一天，一个姓李（LI）的人走近我，问我是否负责《新时代》的出版工作，并询问该刊物的期数。我如实回答，并补充说该刊物已于9月1日停刊。随后李让我在那里待几天，并称他将指派人员进行调查。他还表示，如果发现我没有参与其他任何活动，将允许我离开该地（极司菲尔路76号），但要求我在被拘留期间领会汪精卫先生的事业宗旨。他还交给我两本书，一本是汪精卫著的《和平运动言论》，另一本是周佛海（CHOW FU HAI）著的《回忆与前瞻》。
第二天没有人来找我。
第三天，一个姓谭（TAN）的人来看我，劝我支持汪精卫先生的和平运动，放弃我对抗战的同情。我回答说我会考虑他的建议。
第四天，李再次来看我，并称既然发现我与任何活动无关，我可以在9月27日离开该地。

In the course of an interview at 3 p.m., September
27, LI stated that I was allowed to go and told me
to communicate with him by telephone No. 22812 and
22915, after I had considered his suggestions and also
if I would consult with him in any matter.
Since my release, I have seldom been out nor have
I been communicated with LI.
I was taking my daughter to the Metropol Theatre
this afternoon, and purchased two tickets. As it was
too early, I took my daughter into the Sun Company,
where I met one named SOO ( 苏 ) who is also connected
with 76 Jessfield Road. He wanted me to go to 76
Jessfield Road, but I refused. SOO then detailed a man
to shadow me and after leaving the Sun Company, I was
arrested by C.P.C. 2055 at the request of that man at the
corner of Nanking and Lloyd Roads at 1.10 p.m. I told
the C.P.C. that the man was strange to me and that he
was a kidnapper.

Signed : LI YING ZIAO

在9月27日下午3时的谈话中，李表示允许我离开，并告诉我在考虑他的建议后，以及如果我在任何事项上需要与他商议，可通过电话22812和22915与他联系。
自获释以来，我很少外出，也未与李联系。
今天下午，我带女儿去大都会电影院，买了两张票。因为时间尚早，我带女儿去了先施公司，在那里遇到了一个姓苏（SOO）的人，此人也与极司菲尔路76号有关联。他想让我去极司菲尔路76号，但我拒绝了。随后苏指派一人跟踪我，在我离开先施公司后，下午1时10分，在南京路与劳合路（Lloyd Road）交界处，应那人的要求，我被华捕2055号逮捕。我告诉该华捕，那人我不认识，他是个绑匪。

签名：李英樵

Sir,
At 1.p.m. 27-10-39, C.P.C.2058 brought to Louza
Station a male Chinese named Li Ying Ziau (李印樵) age
30, Peiping, M/unemployed, residing 69 Pakhoi Road, whom
he had arrested at the instigation of one Wong Ching Mow
(黄慶武), Jr., Tungchow, M/agent, residing No.76 Jessfield
Road, for being a Central Government murderer.
Enquiries by D.I. Hutton, J.D.3.394 and the under-
signed show that Li Ying Ziau was formerly the editor of
the Modern Times (新时代) Newspaper, 309 Chungking Road,
which newspaper was closed by order of the Municipal
Council on 1st of September, 1939, for Anti-Wang Ching
Wei (汪精衛) activities.
The former editor when questioned stated that at
about 7.p.m. on 23-9-39 he was having dinner in the
Tsing Loong (晉隆) Chinese Restaurant, 400 Yu Ya Ching
Road, with two male friends when they were joined by
another male Chinese.
Upon finishing the dinner a suggestion was made
that all proceed to the Paramount Ball-room but as the
former editor was unable to dance he declined to go until
persuaded by the other members of the party.
The four men left the restaurant in M/car, Lic.
No.3741, and upon reaching the Paramount Ball-room the
car proceeded along Jessfield Road one of the party claim-
ing that he must change his clothing.
Upon reaching No.76 Jessfield Road the car entered
the premises where the former editor was detained for

先生，
1939年10月27日下午1时，华捕2058号将一名叫李印樵（Li Ying Ziau）的中国男子带至老闸捕房，该男子30岁，北平人，无业，居住于北海路69号。他是受黄庆武（Wong Ching Mow， Jr.，通州人，特工，居住于极司菲尔路76号）的指使被捕的，罪名是中央政府谋杀犯。
经三等甲级侦探（D.I.）哈顿（Hutton，J.D.3.394）及本人的调查表明，李印樵曾是位于重庆路309号的《新时代》（Modern Times）报纸的编辑，该报因从事反汪精卫活动，于1939年9月1日奉工部局命令关闭。
在接受讯问时，前编辑称，1939年9月23日晚7时许，他正在虞洽卿路400号的晋隆（Tsing Loong）中餐馆与两名男性朋友共进晚餐，期间又有另一名中国男子加入。
晚餐结束后，有人提议大家前往百乐门舞厅，但因前编辑不会跳舞，起初拒绝前往，后经同行其他人劝说才同意。
四人乘坐一辆汽车（牌照号码3741）离开餐厅，到达百乐门舞厅后，车辆沿极司菲尔路行驶，同行中一人声称必须更换衣物。
到达极司菲尔路76号后，车辆驶入院内，前编辑在此被拘留

proceed to Jessfield Road, stating that he would later
return and request the handing over of the editor.

该前编辑称，除了被迫睡在地板上外，他在被拘留期间受到了相当不错的待遇。

该编辑称，自获释以来，他未与极司菲尔路76号方面联系。

1939年10月27日中午，该编辑在其9岁女儿李松筠（Li Soong Yung）的陪同下，参观了南京路的先施公司百货商店，在那里他遇到了一个叫苏（Soo）的人，此人是他首次在极司菲尔路76号见到的。

苏与黄庆武在一起，并向巡捕指控该编辑是谋杀犯。当黄庆武陪同该编辑随巡捕前往捕房时，苏离开并前往极司菲尔路，称他稍后将回来并要求移交该编辑。

经向交通股查询，查明汽车牌照号码3741登记在吴永基（Woo Yoong Kyi，原文不清）名下，地址为极司菲尔路119弄28号。
